children: China has purchased around 1M metric tons of U.S. soybeans this week ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s expected visit to the U.S. later this month,

State-owned traders Sinograin and COFCO are believed to have made the latest purchases. One Asia-based trader said Sinograin had been particularly active in recent days, with buying taking place ahead of Xi’s expected U.S. visit.

The buying comes as global oilseed supplies tighten, with inventories in Brazil, the world's largest soybean exporter, declining. The purchases could also help support trade ties between Washington and Beijing ahead of the expected meeting between Xi and U.S. President Donald Trump.
Separately, the U.S. Department of Agriculture on Wednesday reported 340,000 metric tons of U.S. soybean sales to China and another 100,000 metric tons to unidentified destinations.

Following a May meeting between Xi and Trump, Washington said China had agreed to purchase $17B of non-soy U.S. agricultural products annually through 2028 while maintaining its commitment to buy 25M metric tons of U.S. soybeans each year over the same period.
